name: Andy Katz-Mayfield
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Mammoth Brands (formerly Harry's Inc.; owns Harry's, Flamingo, Lume, Mando)
profile: Duke and Stanford GSB (MBA 2011) alum who worked at Bain & Company and Charlesbank Capital before co-founding Harry's with Jeff Raider in 2012. Harry's grew into a ~$750M-revenue DTC/retail razor business; in April 2025 the parent was renamed Mammoth Brands, which he still co-leads with Raider.
interesting_fact: In January 2014, barely a year after launch, Harry's bought the century-old German blade maker Feintechnik (Eisfeld, founded 1920) for $100M so it could control manufacturing; in 2019 Edgewell agreed to buy Harry's for $1.4B before the FTC sued to block it.
deep_cut_fact: His first paying job was as a banquet waiter at a country club, which taught him that great service 'isn't that hard'; he has every Harry's employee spend a day each quarter working in customer experience, and says he wants to build a brand that lasts 100 years.
notes: Co-CEO with Jeff Raider (also Warby Parker co-founder). Best route is Mammoth Brands press email. LinkedIn listed is the company page, not his personal profile.

name: Scott Ringwelski
current_role: Co-founder, Handshake (former CTO; current operating title not publicly stated)
profile: Traverse City, Michigan native and Michigan Tech software-engineering grad ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, with Garrett Lord and Ben Christensen in 2014 and served as its CTO. Handshake was valued at $3.5B in 2022; Ringwelski keeps a low public profile and is listed today simply as co-founder.
interesting_fact: Handshake was born at a small engineering school in Houghton, Michigan: the founders saw the opportunity gap versus Ivy League students; the platform grew to 18M students and 1,200 schools by 2021.
deep_cut_fact: While Lord and Christensen pitched colleges on the road, he stayed in Houghton building the product; he took the call from Wabash College that became Handshake's first client ('my first and only sales call'), and the first HQ was a rental house with a hole where a basement window should be.
notes: Very low public profile; co-founders call him 'the smartest person in all our CS classes'. Current role unclear (Handshake now lists a different CTO). Route via Handshake press or Michigan Tech alumni network.
